_wilmslowPiccolinoCiboSource: Piccolino Grande and Cibo Gran Cafe added 2026-09-18 at explicit user request (named directly: 'piccolino's gran cafe, cibo gran cafe' — the user knows both personally). Both are exactly the case the two-gate model (CLAUDE.md Hard rule 1, 2026-09-16) was built for: real multi-site groups that the old single chain-veto would have excluded outright, now judged on Gate 1/Gate 2 instead. Piccolino Grande, 6-12 Swan Street (postcode SK9 1HE, geocoded via postcodes.io) is part of the national Piccolino chain (Individual Restaurants) — verified via piccolinorestaurants.com, confidentials.com and themanc.com as a GBP 2m, 2026 rebuild described as Piccolino's most ambitious site outside London (marble/brass/terrazzo interior, copper-clad pizza oven, a winterised Tuscan terrace, a tableside 'carbonara grande' and Fassona Piedmontese T-bone). Gate 1: passes cleanly — an upscale, well-regarded premium-casual group, not mass-market high-street. Gate 2 distinctiveness: 3 — CLAUDE.md's own worked example ('a good Piccolino') is this exact case; the flagship-tier rebuild argues for the top of that band rather than a generic 3, but the format is still a familiar national brand, not singular. ownership='group'. Cibo Gran Cafe, 31-33 Grove Arcade (postcode SK9 1DU) is the newer sibling site to the already-seeded Cibo (26-28 Green Lane, two minutes away) — verified via ciborestaurants.co.uk and squaremeal.co.uk as a combined bar/ristorante/artisanal-patisserie format with private event space (90 seated/150 standing) and a Sunday afternoon tea. Researching this site surfaced that Cibo Restaurants is a real 5-site regional group (Manchester, Hale, two Wilmslow sites, Disley), not the single independent restaurant the existing Cibo entry's ownership defaulted to under migration 0009's blanket backfill (distinctiveness=4/ownership='independent' applied to all 244 pre-existing rows) — that default is corrected alongside this addition (ownership -> 'small_group') rather than left silently wrong now that real research contradicts it. Cibo Gran Cafe Gate 1: passes (same small regional group, same quality bar). Gate 2 distinctiveness: 3 — a genuinely less common combined format for the area, but still a recognisable extension of an existing local brand rather than a singular find. ownership='small_group'. Both venues' dietary tags (vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free) are sourced, not assumed: Piccolino's own allergen pages confirm gluten-free pasta and vegan substitutions on request; Cibo Gran Cafe's listings confirm vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free options (though guest feedback on gluten-free handling there is mixed — flagged, not hidden). BRUNCH SPOT (already used for Caramello) reused for Cibo Gran Cafe rather than inventing a new type, since its daytime cafe/patisserie identity fits that tile cleanly. Distinctiveness/ownership values here are documented in this note and applied directly via SQL (supabase/migrations/0013_wilmslow_piccolino_cibo.sql) — not stored as JSON fields on the venue entries below, since no other entry in this file carries those fields yet and adding them to only two would make the schema inconsistent; the live database is the real source of truth for those two columns going forward (see 0010_growth_engine.sql's own source-of-truth-flip note). One more thing surfaced re-reading _wilmslowDensitySource below: its chain-exclusion list from the original August pass (Slug & Lettuce, Revolution, The Botanist, Unico Lounge/The Lounges, Anthology/Greene King, The King William/Robinsons, Stanneylands/JW Lees) is the same kind of list that produced the Mouro Coffee Bar re-evaluation candidate elsewhere — worth a fresh Gate 1/Gate 2 pass, not done as part of this addition.

_dailyReviewPromotionSource20260916: 2026-09-16: curia-suggestion-review's daily pass independently re-verified the 10 candidates in docs/data/venue-suggestions.json with a 2026-09-16 suggestedDate and promoted 8 (Pottery Corner, Chorlton; The Damson Tree Cafe, Cheadle Hulme; Ebenezer's Craft Beer Emporium, Nantwich; St Peter's Church & Norman Chapel, Prestbury; BeefnBerry Bistro, Macclesfield; The Blarney Barrel, Bramhall; The Old Bakery Didsbury; Runway Pilates, Alderley Edge) via fresh independent web search, coordinates re-checked against the sanity box, reason copy checked against Brand voice and left unchanged. One candidate was rejected on fresh-eyes re-verification, reversing the original researcher's own 'single-site, no chain risk' finding: Mouro Coffee Bar (Heaton Moor) is in fact a real, actively expanding four-site coffee brand (the original Heaton Moor site, two Altrincham sites on Oxford Road and Market Street, and a fourth opened 16 May 2026 on Tib Street in the Northern Quarter itself, per themanc.com's own 'Mouro opens third coffee shop' coverage) — well past this file's established 2-3-site small-sibling-group allowance and spanning two separate towns/a city centre, a real chain by Hard rule 1's own standard rather than a family pair; the original candidate's search evidently missed the Altrincham/Tib Street sites entirely. One candidate needed real judgment and was sent to docs/data/pending-review-queue.json rather than decided outright: Underbank (Stockport (Underbanks)) was proposed as a second, distinct venue from this file's own already-promoted 'The Underbank' (2026-09-11, described there as a beer hall run by 'the same husband-and-wife team behind Heaton Moor's Nook'), but fresh re-verification found that description — former bank building, Des and Nina O'Malley, Pomona Island/Runaway on tap, a basement sound system, opened 30 May 2025 — matches the real-world venue actually branded 'Underbank' (no 'The'), not a Benji Taylor-founded live-music venue in the Syndikat building that a different, third search independently confirmed is the real 'The Underbank'. In other words: this file's existing 'The Underbank' entry appears to already describe the new candidate's own venue under the wrong name, and the real 'The Underbank' (Benji Taylor's) has apparently never been seeded at all — a naming/identity mix-up between two real, similarly-named venues on the same street, not a simple duplicate or a simple distinct-venue case, so a human call is needed on whether to rename the existing entry, add the Benji Taylor venue instead, or something else; not promoted or rejected here. Bar Fire Station Social Cucina precedent duplicated: none this run. The three items already sitting in docs/data/pending-review-queue.json (Prana/Altrincham, Buon Cibo/Heaton Moor, Rustik/Didsbury) were checked against Curia Command's pending_review collection (empty, no decision recorded) and left unchanged. Curia Command's pending_review collection had zero decided items to apply this run. The closure-audit rotating slice (indices 95-99: Manchester Craft and Design Centre, The Horsfall, Bar Etna, Knutcraft at the Ruskin Rooms, Mobberley Ice Cream Coffee House) found no closures — all five re-confirmed still trading. See docs/data/districts.json's own 2026-09-16 note for the Chester district promotion from the same run.
_dailyReviewPromotionSource20260917: 2026-09-17: curia-suggestion-review's daily pass hit a genuine research-tool outage for most of this run — WebSearch returned 'unavailable' errors on the majority of queries and, when it did return results, surfaced only Wikipedia-indexed content; WebFetch was EGRESS_BLOCKED for essentially every domain tested (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, Instagram, Facebook, Tripadvisor, Companies House, CAMRA/whatpub, even a direct Wikipedia fetch). Of the 10 pending candidates with a 2026-09-17 suggestedDate (9 for the newly-seeded Chester district, plus Eden in Heaton Moor) and the 4 long-stuck pending-review-queue items (Prana, Buon Cibo, Rustik, the Underbank naming mix-up), only 3 could be genuinely independently re-verified this run: Storyhouse, Chester Cathedral and Grosvenor Museum, all confirmed via Wikipedia's own coverage (the one source WebSearch could still surface) as real, single-site/non-replicable institutions with no closure signal — promoted. One minor factual correction surfaced: Storyhouse's Wikipedia-documented opening date is May 2017, not 2018 as the original candidate's researchNotes stated — not reflected in the promoted reason text, which never cited a year. The remaining 6 Chester candidates (Craft & Company, Beer Heroes, Huxley's, Paysan, Olive Tree Brasserie, Shrub) and Eden (Heaton Moor) could NOT be independently re-verified — none has meaningful Wikipedia coverage, and every other source attempted was blocked — so they stay 'pending', untouched, in venue-suggestions.json rather than being promoted on trust or rejected without evidence; Olive Tree Brasserie in particular (a claimed 3-site regional group spanning Lytham St Annes/Preston/Chester) is flagged as the highest-priority re-check once tooling recovers, since a multi-region footprint is exactly the case Hard rule 1 exists to catch. The 4 long-stuck pending-review-queue items were also left completely unchanged — no new evidence could be found either way for any of them this run, a genuine tooling gap rather than a fresh 'still unresolved' finding. The closure audit could not be performed this run for the same reason (rotating slice, indices 28-32: Wiltons, Franco's, Chris Beetles Gallery, Spencer House, all St James's; The Globe, Olaya) — nothing was written to pending-review-queue.json for it, since no evidence either way was actually found and reporting 'still trading' from memory alone wouldn't meet this rule's own bar. Curia Command's pending_review collection was checked via read_db (unaffected by the outage) and had zero decided items to apply. Flagged for whoever runs this job next: retry the full queue once WebSearch/WebFetch are confirmed working again — today's small promotion (3 of 14 actionable items) reflects a tooling outage, not a thin queue.
